glosses: on the basis of; by the standard of
patterns.usage_note: The standard-marking member: it names the criterion a judgment rests on (所定の基準をもって) or the quality the actor brings to bear (誠意をもって, 責任をもって), presenting it as the authoritative measure. Where the sibling instrumental entry names the medium an act travels through (書面をもって知らせる), this one names what the act is measured by. It descends from をもちて (持つ), is at home in notices, contracts, and ceremonial speech, and carries a separate deadline sense ('as of', 本日をもって閉店) that has nothing to do with either. でもって is its emphatic everyday counterpart and plain で the neutral one.

examples.ruby: 合否[ごうひ]は所定[しょてい]の基準[きじゅん]をもって判定[はんてい]いたします。
examples.english: Pass or fail is determined against the prescribed standard.

examples.ruby: 全[すべ]ての手続[てつづ]きは電子[でんし]署名[しょめい]をもって完了[かんりょう]する。
examples.english: All the paperwork is finalized by electronic signature.

examples.ruby: 弊社[へいしゃ]は誠意[せいい]をもって対応[たいおう]いたします。
examples.english: We will handle the matter in good faith.

patterns.usage_note: An emphatic expansion of the particle で that puts extra weight on the instrument or resource being used; it is at home in speech and relaxed writing rather than in official notices, where をもって is the expected choice. Learners should keep it apart from the sentence-initial conversational connective でもって ('and then'), which is a different animal.

examples.ruby: その問題[もんだい]は結局[けっきょく]お金[かね]でもって解決[かいけつ]した。
examples.english: In the end, that problem got solved with money.

examples.ruby: 彼[かれ]は理屈[りくつ]でもって人[ひと]を説得[せっとく]しようとする。
examples.english: He tries to win people over by sheer logic.

examples.ruby: 新[あたら]しい方法[ほうほう]でもってやり直[なお]してみよう。
examples.english: Let's start over with a new approach.

patterns.usage_note: The plain, unmarked way to name the medium or route by which something is done or delivered — メールで, 窓口で, バスで — and the everyday default against which をもって sounds formal and でもって sounds emphatic. Concrete tools and materials (筆で書く, 布で作る) sit with the sibling instrumental entry. Before a noun it takes the form での (電話での連絡), which is why the dictionary form of the pattern is listed that way.

examples.ruby: 詳[くわ]しい内容[ないよう]はメールでのご案内[あんない]となります。
examples.english: We'll send you the details by email.

examples.ruby: 申[もう]し込[こ]みは窓口[まどぐち]での受付[うけつけ]のみとなります。
examples.english: Applications are taken over the counter only.

examples.ruby: 学校[がっこう]までは毎日[まいにち]バスで通[かよ]っている。
examples.english: I commute to school by bus every day.
